title: fix: unblock canonical model permission migration
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes migration 0062's D1 CPU failure in [production run 34137739809](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations/actions/runs/34137739809): replaces 159 full-table updates with one direct update and a shared rename lookup. All 159 reviewed mapping pairs are unchanged.
- Preserves community/unknown IDs, unrelated permissions, order, deduplication, and retry safety. Adds coverage for all renames in one allowlist.
- Deploys Gen when 0062 changes, so this migration-only repair completes both worker deployments and the required final cleanup.
- Verified on staging through `wrangler d1 migrations apply`, not file import: 200,000 synthetic keys / 100,000 affected, 18.32s database time, zero mismatches. Late-writer cleanup and repeat execution passed; synthetic tables removed. Full Enter suite: 1,113 passing tests. Workflow tests, formatting and Enter typecheck pass.
- Rollout: merge into main, promote to production, then verify migration, Enter/Gen deployments and final cleanup. No model definitions, SDK, Reddit, secrets or production data changed by this PR preparation.

gist.headline: The migration stops stampeding
gist.blurb: Model permission migration 0062 traded 159 laps around the database for one direct update and a shared rename map. Same carefully reviewed permissions, considerably less CPU drama.
gist.summary: Reworked Enter migration 0062 to replace 159 full-table model-permission updates with one direct update plus a shared rename lookup, preserving all 159 mappings, unknown IDs, permission ordering, deduplication, and retry safety.
gist.impact: Production D1 migrations can now standardize canonical model permissions efficiently—including late-writer cleanup—while deploying both Enter and Gen for the completed migration rollout.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful migration gardener pruning 159 tangled permission vines into one neat labeled path leading to a cozy D1 database planter. A CRT monitor robot can happily watch a small terminal report a successful cleanup, while model-name seedlings remain intact to represent preserved mappings and data safety.
